I have a R9 380 and whenever I play video games, it makes the room heat up too much. My older card didn't do this. Why is my new card heating up the room so much? My card is an msi card.
Computer gets too hot playing games
So, to be clear, the PC isn't overheating, it's just making your room warmer than your old card did? Are you running games at higher graphical settings now? What was your old card?

The best answer is that your new card gets much hotter than your old card, and it's creating additional strain on your power supply (PSU) as well. It's also possible that your new card, with it's higher graphical settings, are putting additional strain on the CPU. What was the original graphics card, and what PSU do you have?
My old graphics card was a radeon HD 7770. I use a 430W power supply. My CPU is AMD so that might raise power usage a lot also.

Yep, that 7770 uses ~86 Watts, while the R9 380 uses ~196 Watts. That alone is equivalent to an additional 110 Watt bulb pumping heat into the room under load. That puts additional strain on your PSU which causes it to heat up as well.

Also, while you may be fine for a while, you really should replace the PSU. The recommended PSU for an r9 380 is 550W. If the current PSU fails it could damage additional components.

A typical light bulb is 60 watts. You graphics card alone is a little over two light bulbs, plus your CPU is another light bulb, and LCD monitors have a few light bulbs behind the panel, not to mention the hard drives. You basically have 6-10 light bulbs in your room that are generating heat (which, if you've ever touched one...get really hot). Same thing happens to my room with my GTX 980. I have to keep my door and window open all the time to keep air circulating, otherwise my room will turn into an oven.

This is normal. Only way to fix it, in this case, is to get a less powerful GPU.
Or go full Linus and find a way to vent the heat out of the room, because that was such a good idea...

While I think some of those controversial submissions he's done maybe weren't that intentional, for me it looks like some definitely are. And those eye pokes in his last fight.. Seems like he's going from bad to worse.

Also, I'd love to hear input from those who actually train BJJ, I don't myself. Are they really so controversial as it seems and media lets us to believe? It's a different thing to judge from your armchair when you have never been in those situations yourself compared to actually being there yourself.
Do you find Paul Harris (Rousimar Palhares) to be dirty and if so, should he be allowed to fight in the future?

In BJJ, you're taught to let go while rolling and/or wait for the referee to stop the match in competition without cranking a locked in submission. I've dealt with guys who've tried to break and tear shit, and they're frowned upon within the community. Leg locks are a big issue, as most schools don't teach them because of how dangerous they are, and way too many people don't know how to properly defend those. When going over kneebars, heelhooks, straight ankles, etc, you go super slow when drilling because of the high risk of injury with them.

What Palhares has done over the years should've been addressed a long time ago. Cranking on submissions over and over again puts lots of fighters in serious danger. He's got a history of this in MMA and BJJ, so it's really not media hype,. The guy needs to be banned from MMA. He hasn't learned his lesson at all.
Exactly the kind of informative answer I was hoping for. Many thanks!

I absolutely agree, he seems either too stupid or too emotional to learn.

Either way, it's not hype, it's been proven time and again that he's not capable of fighting without trying to injure someone purposely.

There is no place for him in the sport.

I don't train, but have seen many fights of his. In most of his fights he holds on to the submission well after the ref calls the fight over. It was perfectly clear that his opponents tapped out and the ref was trying to pry him off on numerous occasions, so yeah, he's a dirty fighter no doubt about it. If it's clear to anyone watching him fight that he's a dirty fighter, why do they allow him to continue?

I have definitely been thinking he's dirty for a long time. But I also wanted to hear it from those who train what they think about it just to be 100% sure that what he does is what I think it is, therefore this question :). And yeah, agreed. He should be banned for life.

I'm not a BJJ practitioner but I am a kickboxer. I think it's the same principle as wailing on someone's head when they're already down and out - you're taking it past a competition and more in to "actual assault" territory imo. Eye poking is also a very clear indicator that the guy isn't just making mistakes or holding locks until the referee stops it- he's just a prick.

I just have been thinking is there something like, you maybe don't feel the tap and hold on until the referee comes on etc in some of those cases what he does what only BJJ practitioner can understand so that's why I asked. For me it looks like definitely intentional but it wouldn't be the first time when I form my opinion, then actually understand that it's not what it actually seems like when I have been talking with someone who can explain it to me because they have experience and knowledge about the topic.

Well the other thing about holding locks etc is that there's a difference between holding and cranking - when you feel the tap I can forgive just holding the lock until the referee stops it (after all, there has been times when people have tapped in UFC and then gone on like nothing happened)...
